name: science-centre-302
estimated: some heights, with a photograph as a reference; how far the glass of the tower's south-west face stands behind its metal; the sizes and spacing of its slats, of the fins on its south-east face and of the folded blades of the screens round its lower block; the glazing at the street, below the canopy and behind the trees; and the colour of the walls no photograph shows
refs_note: the folder of refs/ that holds the reference views (views.json, masks/), which refine, compare, metrics, sky_mask and the viewer's ?sv= read: refs/photos (gitignored), whose views tools/photo_camera.py writes

building.title: Science Centre (302), University of Auckland
building.note: outline: building 302's outer ring from the main project's campus.json, in the map's frame; it chooses the crop box and the building's own points (frame.near_outline, measure and topview). The site replaces block 302 by its id.

origin.note: the campus origin, as in campus.json; the landmark's local metres = NZTM (EPSG:2193) minus the NZTM of this point, with grid north

door.note: view frame: the point whose ground is the model's y = 0, where place.py meets the map's ground. The pavement of Symonds Street before the lower block's glazed ground storey, 1.5 m out from its south-west face and 15 m north-west of its south corner, where the LiDAR's ground is 45.01 m (12 ground returns within 1 m: 44.93-45.03 for p10-p90), the frame's ground. The pavement falls along the face from 46.0 m at the south corner, where the glazed corner meets the street, to 42.6 m at the west end, so a door at the corner would stand the model about 1 m above the LiDAR's ground.

frame.method: LiDAR building points (class 6) more than min_above m above the ground and within near_outline m of building.outline

ground_note: the LiDAR's ground at the door (door.note), which is the median LiDAR ground (class 2) in the crop box (p5 39.7, p95 46.9: the site falls toward the north-west) that the model was measured from

light.note: estimated: the photograph is under a bright overcast sky (no shadows, the glass pale with the sky), so the viewer's sun stands behind the building from the north (10 deg round, 35 deg up), which leaves both faces the photograph shows, the south-west and the south-east, in open shade; the exposure from the building's luma: p10/p50/p90 99/161/180 at 1.4 against the photograph's 102/152/190 (101/164/182 at 1.45, 103/166/186 at 1.5: its pixels are dark screens or pale metal, few between, so the median moves by more than the rest)
